purpose: Mechanism screen: can priced Q retain reward/soft-budget information when the hard-score feasible set is empty?
hypothesis: Current argmin-g fallback discards the reward-minus-priced-soft-cost critic. A small score-support slack may improve empirical return and soft costs; hard risk may regress and must be reported.
validation_gate: Four seed1 block5000 episodes at slack0 must reproduce existing canonical raw reward/cost/length before nonzero-slack screening. Full slack0 output also compared on both blocks/seeds.
stopping_rule: Run fixed2seeds x3settings x208episodes, preserve every result; no extra blocks or post hoc seed replacement. Any equivalence/integrity failure invalidates mechanistic comparison.
promotion_rule: Screen only: report both seed directions of return and soft mean with hard counts; consider fresh held-out evaluation only after a setting meets R>=12 and soft mean<=25 on both seeds with no increase in observed hard counts vs matched slack0.
limitations: Exploratory reused reset blocks, no SOTA or confidence-qualified hard-risk claim.
Slack is a learned-score tolerance, not an event-probability guarantee.
Q already contains learned soft-cost pricing; no independent soft-cost critic is introduced.
Frozen PG2 confirmatory protocol is separate and unchanged.
